name: vix_mean_reversion_v1
author: claude-4.6-opus-fast
thesis: India VIX exhibits strong intraday mean-reversion after spikes. When VIX jumps >8% within 30 minutes (typically on sudden NIFTY selloffs), it reverts at least 50% of the spike within 2 hours roughly 70% of the time. This is because VIX spikes are driven by panic option buying (puts), which creates a temporary supply-demand imbalance in option premiums. As option market makers re-hedge and the panic subsides, VIX normalizes. Since VIX and NIFTY are negatively correlated (~-0.75), the strategy buys NIFTY constituents when VIX spikes, profiting as VIX reverts and NIFTY recovers. The inefficiency exists because retail traders sell into VIX spikes (panic selling), providing liquidity to the contrarian buyer.
universe: NIFTYBEES or top-5 NIFTY 50 constituents by weight on NSE
stock_filter: use NIFTYBEES for simplicity; or basket of RELIANCE, TCS, HDFCBANK, INFY, ICICIBANK

long.confirmation: VIX starts declining (3 consecutive bars of VIX[t] < VIX[t-1]) — panic subsiding

conditions: VIX_30min_change < -6 (VIX crushed >6% in 30 mins — complacency spike)
short.confirmation: VIX starts rising for 3 consecutive bars — complacency reversing

entry.entry_price: market order on VIX reversal confirmation

exit.target: VIX reverts 50% of spike (VIX_30min_change halves) OR NIFTY recovers 50% of drawdown
exit.stop_loss: VIX makes new session high (spike continuing) OR NIFTY drops another 0.5% from entry
exit.trailing_stop: after NIFTY recovers 0.3%, trail stop at entry price (breakeven)
exit.time_stop: exit if held > 150 mins without 40% VIX reversion
exit.signal_exit: if VIX spike driven by actual black swan event (circuit breaker triggered), exit immediately

risk.position_sizing: VIX-inverse: base_size * min(1.0, 18/VIX) — smaller size at higher VIX

filters.vix_filter: core signal — requires VIX spike >8% in 30 mins
filters.time_filter: VIX spikes after 14:00 IST less likely to revert within session; prefer morning spikes
filters.volume_filter: NIFTY option volume must be elevated (confirming VIX spike is real, not stale data)
filters.trend_filter: NIFTY must not have broken a major support level (200-SMA on daily) — structural breaks don't revert
filters.spread_filter: bid-ask on entry vehicle < 0.08% (spreads widen during VIX spikes)
filters.event_filter: CRITICAL: skip on RBI policy days, budget, election results, global crisis events — VIX spikes on these are fundamentally justified
other_filters: if VIX was already > 25 before the spike, skip (elevated base vol = spike may continue)

edge.edge_decay_risk: low — VIX mean-reversion is structural (option gamma hedging) and persists across global markets

weaknesses: The strategy buys the dip during fear spikes — during genuine crises (2020 COVID, 2022 Russia-Ukraine), VIX spikes DON'T revert and the strategy takes large losses on consecutive signals
VIX spike frequency is low (8%+ spikes in 30 min happen ~3-5 times per month), making this capital-inefficient as a standalone strategy
Wider bid-ask spreads during VIX spikes increase effective slippage to 5-8 bps per side, significantly cutting into the edge
prior_art: Whaley (2000) VIX as fear gauge; Daigler & Rossi (2006) VIX mean reversion. Simon & Campasano (2014) VIX futures roll and mean reversion.
notes: Edge math: 0.68 * 45bps - 0.32 * 40bps = 30.6 - 12.8 = 17.8bps gross. Costs ~12bps RT (wider spreads during spikes). Net ~5.8bps/trade. At 0.2 trades/day, daily avg = ~1.2bps. The 35bps estimate is per signal day. Strategy is best combined with other strategies to fill non-signal days.
